message.content:
Hydrogen (H) – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has several distinctive properties:

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Common isotope** | Protium (^1H) – 99.98 % natural abundance |
| **Other stable isotopes** | Deuterium (^2H, D) – ~0.015 %; Tritium (^3H) – radioactive, half‑life ≈12.32 yr |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average weighted by natural isotopic composition) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ (negative, meaning energy is released when an electron is added) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) at 1 atm |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) at 1 atm |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 kg m⁻³) |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| **State at room temperature** | Diatomic gas (H₂) |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (range 4–75 % by volume) |
| **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂), reacts with halogens (HX), oxidizes to water or oxides under suitable conditions |
| **Bonding** | Typically forms covalent bonds; in H₂ the two electrons form a single σ bond |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – fundamental to astrophysical spectroscopy |
| **Uses** | Fuel cell technology, ammonia synthesis (Haber process), rocket propellant (liquid hydrogen), laboratory reagent, hydrogenation reactions |

These values capture hydrogen’s essential physical and chemical characteristics, including its isotopic variants and typical behavior in both laboratory and industrial contexts.
